sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: 'Quality Checks' row 54 (#53 task_is_distinct_and_authored) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 54 (no additional annotation in columns E onward)
Sibling comparison: projects/threadline-chat/threadline-chat/{instruction.md,task.toml,tests/rubric/browser/browser.toml criterion ids}; task.toml category/description of every task under projects/
evidence: The task is authored for a specific product (Kittle & Rowe law-firm client chat) whose core mechanics are domain-specific and absent from every sibling: ethical walls that must hold across list/thread/search snippets/reply quotes/unread/mentions/message-link previews/transcripts and take effect live (environment/instructions/walls-and-retention.md 'Who sees a matter'), per-matter disappearing-message timers measured from stored send time against a fixed firm clock with irreversible deletion (same file 'Disappearing messages'; integration.md fixed clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z), partner-only legal holds scoped to exactly one message that override timers and block author deletion, and matter transcripts listing held-edited versions and deleted-with-replies placeholders. Seed data is legal-domain (matters M-11 'Pryce lease dispute', M-12 'Marsh Holdings acquisition', M-13 'Pryce will'; Dev walled from M-12; partner/associate/client roles). Scored criteria mirror this domain: wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live, deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes, hold_scope_and_release, search_and_transcript, retention_marks, transcript_page. The only messaging sibling in projects/ is threadline-chat (Slack-style workspace: channels, DMs, reactions, pins, presence/typing, incoming webhooks, moderation, pagination; criteria such as direct_message_pair_uniqueness_and_authorization, timeline_pagination_preserves_position). Kittle has none of DMs, reactions, pins, presence, webhooks or pagination, and Threadline has no walls, timers, holds or transcripts. Shared generic chat conventions (stale-edit refusal, idempotent send, per-user unread, replies) are genre mechanics expressed differently (Kittle: 3-level nested replies with quotes, 'new messages' line, mark-unread, mention suggestions limited to matter viewers), not a renamed criterion set; solution server.js has 51 wall/hold/timer/transcript references and 0 channel/webhook references. Other tasks in projects/ are different domains (marketplace, insurance claims, recruiting, games, editors, etc.). Domain-plan fit: task.toml metadata category 'Messaging & Chat Interfaces', arena_slice 'full-stack-express-sqlite-messaging-chat-kittle-matter-chat', provenance 'Messaging and chat interfaces package', and the description truthfully summarise the product. Side observation for the owner/the config row, not a defect of this row: the staged contract and template-era guidance list metadata category = "programming" (staged-task-contract.md task.toml block; NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:82) while this task uses the assigned domain string; NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:82 itself tells authors to describe the assigned domain accurately, so this belongs to the metadata/contract rows. Adversarial check: a nouns-swapped Threadline clone (channels renamed matters, private-channel membership renamed walls) would fail this row because it would lack timers/holds/transcripts and live wall imposition; conversely, a conforming alternative is not penalised by this row since it judges task authorship, not app implementation. No runtime evidence is required for this row; absence of full configured judge runs (raw-evidence-index.json scope) does not bear on distinctness.
